text:
jia: ran a short perf run against the 8k-seq workload; seeing repeated kernel handoffs when continuous-batching mixes 1-3 token tails with long seqs. pprof attached.

sam: can you paste the flamegraph snippet? curious if it's kernel launch or kv warm.

jia: here's the key slice:
```
# pprof cpu
flat  cum   name
0.25s 1.11s launch_kernel
0.20s 0.70s kv_lookup
0.12s 0.40s continuous_batcher::dispatch
```

oliver: hm launch_kernel is high. are we switching kernels per sequence-length within the same batch?

jia: yes. autotuner picks small-kernel for tails then switches to wide-kernel for long seqs; that switch allocates new stream and warms KV -> extra 3-8ms.

tara: so the mixing causes more launches than a pure-long or pure-short batch. any request-level routing we can do?

sam: maybe add a hysteresis: prefer existing kernel if >X requests in-flight for that kernel, or threshold by cumulative tokens.

jia: tried simple hysteresis: reduced switches by ~60% in microbench but end-to-end p90 only improved 10% — KV warm still leaks.

oliver: what's the KV cache miss profile? small tails evict often?

jia: exact numbers: tail-heavy batches had kv_miss_rate 18%, long-only 4%. eviction churn is the culprit.

infra-bot: deploy triggered: perf-hotfix/hysteresis-2 -> staging

tara: could we batch by inferred seqlen bucket in the scheduler (soft bucketing) to reduce heterogeneity without hurting latency for small requests?

sam: that's the idea I sketched earlier. add a lightweight seqlen hint in the request header and prefer same-bucket coalescing for 10ms window.

jia: prototype looks promising: switch count down 72%, kv_miss_rate down to 8%, p95 improved ~22% on synthetic mix.

oliver: tradeoff is a few small reqs wait extra 8-12ms. acceptable if overall p95 for customer improves. add metrics to track per-bucket wait.

tara: add per-route config toggle so we can A/B for dedicated customers. file an RFC?

sam: i'll draft RFC and include a perf experiment plan. jia please upload traces and the pprof snippets to the RFC.

jia: done. uploading to the RFC now. thanks all :rocket:
